# Sesam starts the command directly, forwards signals addressed only to itself,
# and waits for the child to terminate.

exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'
exec sesam init --user admin
cp raw-fixture raw.txt
exec sesam add raw.txt
rm raw.txt

exec runprobe signals 15 sesam run --secret RAW=raw.txt -- runprobe hold RAW
stdout 'parent signals=\[15\] child terminated and reaped'
exec runprobe no-temp-files

exec runprobe signals 1 sesam run --secret RAW=raw.txt -- runprobe hold RAW
stdout 'parent signals=\[1\] child terminated and reaped'
exec runprobe no-temp-files

# SIGINT and SIGQUIT are not forwarded: a terminal delivers them to the whole
# process group already. Sent to sesam alone they change nothing, and the child
# only terminates on the later SIGTERM.
exec runprobe signals 2 15 sesam run --secret RAW=raw.txt -- runprobe hold RAW
stdout 'parent signals=\[2 15\] child terminated and reaped'
exec runprobe signals 3 15 sesam run --secret RAW=raw.txt -- runprobe hold RAW
stdout 'parent signals=\[3 15\] child terminated and reaped'

# A terminal Ctrl-C reaches sesam and the child at once; sesam reports the
# child's status.
exec runprobe signals group 2 sesam run --secret RAW=raw.txt -- runprobe hold RAW
stdout 'parent signals=\[2\] child terminated and reaped'
exec runprobe no-temp-files

# SIGKILL cannot be forwarded. The orphan keeps its own secret descriptor.
exec runprobe signals 9 sesam run --secret RAW=raw.txt -- runprobe hold RAW parent-gone
stdout 'parent signal=9 child survived and reparented; secret descriptor still readable'
exec runprobe no-temp-files

! exists raw.txt
exec sesam id
stdout '^admin$'

-- raw-fixture --
raw
